title: FERC General Correspondence — Docket P-7887-000: Letter to Ashuelot River Hydro Inc. discussing the 07/15/2026 Dam Safety Inspection, Emergency Action Plan and Status Report etc. for the Minnewawa Project under P-7887.
text:
FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION
Office of Energy Projects
Division of Dam Safety and Inspections – New York Regional Office
Telephone No. (212) 273-5900
September 1, 2026
via Electronic Mail
Mr. Justin D. Ahmann
Ashuelot River Hydro, Inc.
justin@apec-mt.com
RE: Letter to Ashuelot River Hydro, Inc. discussing the July 15, 2026 Dam Safety
Inspection, reviewing Emergency Action Plan & Status Report and Owners Dam Safety
Program & Annual Review, and requesting penstock inspection plan &schedule for the
Minnewawa Project under P-7887.
Dear Mr. Ahmann,
Thank you for your assistance during our inspection of the project. As a result of the
inspection and in preparation of our Dam Safety Inspection Report, the following items are
noted:
1. Trees and brush were observed to be obscuring portions of the rock along the
abutments, groins, toe, and area just downstream of the dam, particularly on the right
side. As discussed, please remove these trees and brush from project works.
2. Please note that NHDES Dam Safety and Inspection accompanied us on this
inspection and may have additional comments for consideration.
We appreciate your continued cooperation with the dam safety program. If you have
any questions, please contact Shamus Lefchak, P.E. at shamus.lefchak@ferc.gov or at
(212) 273-5914.
In accordance with the timelines discussed in the attached summary, please file the
Annual P12D Status Update, EAP, and plan & schedule for penstock inspection & report
using the Commission’s eFiling system at https://www.ferc.gov/ferc-online/overview.
When eFiling, select Hydro: Dam Safety and New York Regional Office from the eFiling
menu. The cover page of the filing must indicate that the material was eFiled. For assistance
with eFiling, contact FERC Online Support at FERCOnlineSupport@ferc.gov, (866) 208-3676
(toll free), or (202) 502-8659 (TTY).
Sincerely,
John Spain, P.E.
Regional Engineer

P-7887-NH Attachment 1
Summary of Dam Safety Submittals
Annual Status Update - Part 12D Recommendations
In accordance with 18 CFR § 12.41, the annual status report for all Independent
Consultant’s (IC) recommendations that are outstanding/ongoing or were completed since
the previous update was due March 31, 2026 (and is now past due). The status report
should incorporate applicable comments from our review letter issued February 6, 2025.
Emergency Action Plan (EAP) and Requirements
By eFiling received on February 24, 2026, the Exemptee submitted an update to the EAP
for the project. We have reviewed the submitted EAP and have the following comments:
1. We understand that video cameras were installed to provide real-time monitoring at
the dam. Please update the EAP to account for any changes in event verification
and response procedures as a result of the camera installation, including what
entities are automatically notified following verification (such as first-impacted
residents, SW NH Fire Mutual Aid, MPD, etc). Please also update the Sudden
Failure / Time Sensitive Assessment accordingly.
2. We recommend that Section IV define Non-Failure and High Flow dam safety
emergency level categories (in addition to Potential Failure and Imminent Failure),
as recommended in Section 6-3.2.2-2-E of our Engineering Guidelines. It also may
be helpful to more explicitly call out the four EAP response steps defined in the
same Guidelines section.
3. Please include a verification form confirming the Licensee’s understanding of
agreed-upon responsibilities (a sample is provided in Appendix 6-E of our
Engineering Guidelines).
4. Add a section describing the project’s EAP Training and Exercise Program. This
section should identify training received by the individuals who implement the
EAP, training frequency (at least annually), and proposed schedule of exercises
(seminars, workshops, drills, publicized tests of emergency siren, etc.).
Please file a revised EAP by December 31, 2026. Additionally, we received an EAP
Status Report on February 24, 2026, stating that an annual seminar, along with a drill &
call down of contacts from the notification flowchart were conducted on December 19,
2025. You reported that emergency equipment tests were conducted on April 4 and
August 15, 2025. We have no comments on the Status Report.
A Tabletop Exercise was last conducted on March 5, 2025. The Licensee submitted an
Evaluation Report for the Tabletop Exercise on May 5, 2025.

P-7887-NH Attachment 1
Dam Safety Performance Monitoring Program
By eFiling received on February 28, 2025, the Licensee submitted an updated DSSMP
that was accepted by our letter issued December 29, 2025.
By eFiling received on February 17, 2026, the Licensee submitted the 2025 DSSMR that
was reviewed by our letter issued February 23, 2026.
Public Safety Plan (PSP)
By letter received May 5, 2020, the Licensee submitted an updated PSP. We acknowledged
receipt of the PSP without comment in our letter issued May 14, 2020.
Owners Dam Safety Program (ODSP)
By eFiling received on February 24, 2026, you submitted the results of ODSP annual
review and ODSP update. We have reviewed theses submittals and have no comment at
this time.
Other Dam Safety Items
Penstock Inspection and Report
IC Recommendation No. 9 from the Periodic Inspection Report recommended performing
penstock thickness measurements along Old Chesam Road by March 2026. Your plan
and schedule submitted June 18, 2024, indicated that the the inspection would be completed
by February 2026. In our letter issued February 6, 2025, we advised that the inspection
should include the full length of the penstock and report thickness measurements, structural
computations, a condition assessment, recommended maintenance measures, expected
service life, and a statement that the features are safe for continued operation (if applicable).
Please confirm if the penstock inspection has been performed or submit a revised plan and
schedule for its completion in the next 60 days. We recommend scheduling a call with
our office to discuss the scope of the inspection before commencing any field work.
